Subject: Short-window surge this weekend — temporary quota increase & billing?

Hi Jonas,

We have a marketing-driven spike coming the week of Aug 21st for a new personalization rollout. Forecasted delta is ~45–60M extra tokens over a 72-hour window (peaks on day 2).

Two quick questions:
- Can Redwood lift our short-window quota for that weekend (one-off, region: us-east) and how fast can that be enabled?
- How will this be billed if we take a temporary burst allowance — are there pre-pay options, or will it show as an overrun at standard PAYG rates?

I attached a small usage snapshot from our staging runs (usage_snapshot_20260815.csv) to give you a sense of traffic profile. We should be able to commit to a PO within 24–48 hours if we get the right pricing.

Subject: Re: Short-window surge this weekend — temporary quota increase & billing?

Hi Claire — thanks for the snapshot, that helps. Short answer: yes, we can support a short-window quota lift quickly, with two pragmatic commercial approaches depending on how you want the accounting to look.

Option A — Prepaid burst pool (recommended for short spikes)
- We allocate a one-time burst credit pool (token budget) for the 72-hour window.
- Blended burst rate: $0.00009 / token for the pool (example math below).
- Credits invoiced up-front or net-30 depending on PO timing; unused credits will be carried as a one-time credit until month end.

Option B — Provisional monthly commit bump
- Temporarily raise your committed throughput for the billing month; overage priced at committed band rates.
- Requires a short amendment to the master SOW for the month; visible as a commit change on the invoice.

Rough numbers based on the CSV: 50M tokens -> burst pool cost ~= $4,500 at the blended rate above. If you want to keep per-token parity with current commit pricing I can run that variant too.

Next steps I propose:
1) Choose A or B (A is fastest — we can enable within 6 hours of payment instructions).
2) If A, procurement sends PO or we send an invoice for the agreed amount and enable the pool on activation.
3) If B, we'll loop Legal for a 1-month amendment (short lead time but possible).

I filed a HubSpot note under deal HW-89231 with the snapshot (https://app.hubspot.com/deal/89231). Ben — can you send a short quote for Option A (prepay) with two tiered discounts (standard vs ~10% sponsor discount) so Claire can share with procurement?

Jonas

Claire — looping in with two compact pricing options + an attached example invoice line.

Option 1 (Fastest) — Prepaid burst pool (72-hr window)
- Token pool: 250,000 credits (can scale up)
- Unit price: $0.00009 / token (blended) -> example: 50,000,000 tokens = $4,500
- Sponsor discount (one-time): 10% (if approved by 8/17 EOD) -> $4,050
- Activation: within 6 hours of invoice confirmation or PO

Option 2 — Temporary commit bump (monthly)
- Raise commit for Aug by 20% for billing month
- Overrun priced at commit-band rates, no upfront payment but requires amendment to SOW
- Depending on final commit level, effective cost may be lower for sustained usage beyond the 72-hr window.

Notes:
- We can prorate a blended invoice line so accounting sees a single row labelled: "Temporary burst credit — Aug 21–23". I attached a sample quote (provisional_burst_quote_v3.pdf).
- If procurement needs net-30 we can proceed but activation will wait for PO processing; if they can pre-pay we enable immediately.
- Legal quick review required for Option 2; minimal amendment.

If Option 1 works, send PO to billing@redwood.com and we'll push the activation and provide a confirmation email with the token pool id.
